{{Quote|I am the protector of that tome you so casually call your own. I am its guardian against the ravages of time. Without me that collection of molecules would have crumbled into dust a thousand years ago.|The spirit protector, to Shas Dovos|<ref name="totjc" />}}
For more than a thousand [[Standard year/Legends|years]], the malevolent [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] of a long-[[Death/Legends|dead]] [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]] served as the protector of an ancient [[Sith spellbook/Legends|spellbook]] forgotten within a hidden [[Sith armory|armory]] of [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] lore deep in the jungles of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]]. Several years before the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], the book over which the '''spirit protector''' maintained stewardship was discovered by a young [[Metalsmith/Legends|blacksmith]] named [[Warb Null|Shas Dovos]]. The [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] specter corrupted Dovos and [[Sith training|taught]] its unsuspecting [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] for more than a decade until finally, under the Master's secret guidance, the blacksmith created a suit of [[Armor/Legends|armor]] imbued with [[Sith sorcery/Legends|Sith magic]]. The spirit then revealed itself and its true plan to restore the lost glory of the [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]]. It renamed the apprentice Warb Null and descended upon him with the [[Magic/Legends|magical]] [[Armor/Legends|armor]], binding man to metal through the power of the dark side of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].

==Biography==
===Steward===
{{Quote|It is I who decide who is worthy to discover this lore. It is I alone who decide how the knowledge will be used.|The spirit protector|<ref name="totjc" />}}
The [[Force ghost/Legends|spirit]] of a [[Death/Legends|deceased]] [[Sith Master/Legends|Sith Master]] resided within the pages of a [[Sith spellbook/Legends|book]] of [[Sith sorcery/Legends|sorcery]], to which it was also confined. The object of the spirit's [[Prison/Legends|imprisonment]] was also its charge, and for more than a thousand [[Standard year/Legends|years]] it protected the volume from the adversities of [[Time/Legends|time]] and toil alike. Unable to personally partake in restoration of the fabled [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empire]] of antiquity, the ghost hoped to one day encounter an individual whom it deemed worthy of its power. More than a decade before the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]], the spirit protector permitted the discovery of its literary accommodation, when a young [[Metalsmith/Legends|blacksmithing]] student named [[Warb Null|Shas Dovos]] happened upon the tome in an ancient [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] [[Sith armory|bunker]] hidden deep in the jungles of the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]]. Dovos stole the book, and the spirit protector recognized in him the potential to become its unwitting servant.<ref name="totjc" />

For more than ten years the spirit protector obscured its clandestine exploitation as it [[Sith training|taught]] Dovos&mdash;albeit slowly and unconsciously&mdash;the intricacies of [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Magic/Legends|magic]]. Nominal amounts of knowledge were imparted in such a manner that Dovos forsook all other aspects of life as he pursued the ancient spirit's wisdom. The protector routinely embellished the [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice's]] dreams with suggestions of destined greatness realized through fruit born of his profession and given strength through the rituals of ancient Sith sorcery. Numerous attempts to craft an object of power were met with failure until, on the fourth evening of one such endeavor, the spirit protector's apprentice completed his masterpiece: a [[Color/Legends|blackened]] suit of [[Armor/Legends|armor]] imbued with the dark side of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]].<ref name="totjc" />

===Treachery===
{{Quote|Do not worry, my disciple. You will have your place in the history of the galaxy. I did not bring you this far to end your albeit insignificant existence now. No, you will become an extension of me. You will go where I cannot and help restore the glory of the Sith.|The spirit protector|<ref name="totjc" />}}
[[File:TOTJ_FNU1.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Warb Null, clad in the armor inspired by the spirit protector]]
At first hesitant to make use of his creation, Dovos' misgivings were quickly eroded by the innuendos of the spirit protector, through whose mental coercion Dovos' confidence in his own fine craftsmanship was restored. Bewildered by the mental intrusion, Dovos cried out as the spirit protector, appearing before him as cinders, confessed its involvement in the blacksmith's affairs since he had found the spellbook in the jungles of his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. With a burst of energy, the spirit protector changed its [[Alien/Legends|alien]]&ndash;like shape into that of a fiercely-expressive [[near-Human]]; it then advanced upon and commended its terrified thrall for doing exactly as it had commanded. The ability to comprehend the spellbook and the subsequent creation of the [[Armor/Legends|armor]] had been the spirit protector's design all along, and, but for its involvement, the young blacksmith would have been otherwise incapable on all fronts. Nevertheless, the spirit demanded remuneration for its granted endowments; Dovos had to become an extension of its will, to further the protector's agenda where and whence it could not.<ref name="totjc" />

Oblivion was the apprentice's expectation, but the spirit protector assured him that destiny had reserved a special place in history for him: Dovos was to participate in the restoration of the long-forgotten Sith Empire. Before he could perform his new task, however, the spirit protector needed to empower Dovos and chose the armor as the means by which he would do so. To symbolize his rebirth, Shas Dovos was renamed by the spirit protector "Warb Null," which it thought suited a being whose new existence was to be an amalgam of flesh and metal. It then swarmed Null and, with the power of Sith magic, bound him to his armor&mdash;the crowning achievement of his former existence.<ref name="totjc" /> Null went on to become a [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] and was selected to serve as the guardian of another Force entity, the spirit of the long-dead [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Freedon Nadd]],<ref name="TOTJA">[[Tales of the Jedi (audio drama)|''Tales of the Jedi'' audio drama]]</ref> in whose name he participated in an attempted [[Freedon Nadd Uprising|revival]] of Sith prominence,<ref name="FNU">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising 1|''Tales of the Jedi – The Freedon Nadd Uprising'' 1]]</ref> exactly as [[Force vision/Legends|predicted]] by the spirit protector.<ref name="totjc" />

Thousands of years later, the failed Jedi Padawan [[Malleus|Telloti Cillmam'n]] discovered Null's armor on the planet [[Nicht Ka]]. When he tried to take the armor's lightsaber, the suit seemed to come to life and clamped his wrist, and when he finally managed to rip the lightsaber from the suit's grasp, the armor fell over onto the floor. A cloud of bone dust was released into the air, and when Cillmam'n unintentionally breathed it in, he was subjected to visions of the past&mdash;memories of a warrior from the time of Adas, as well as Shas Dovos's creation of the armor, his corruption by the spirit protector, and his time as Warb Null. The dark side within the armor corrupted Cillmam'n, leading him to [[Duel on Nicht Ka|kill]] his companions and assume the name Malleus.<ref name="Hammer">{{InsiderCite|147|Hammer (short story)}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|At first your arrogance annoyed me, but eventually I saw how I could put it to use.|The spirit protector, to Shas Dovos|<ref name="totjc" />}}
The spirit protector first appeared to Shas Dovos as a hovering gout of predominately red flame, occasionally accented by violent flares of yellow ember. Afterward it assumed the form of an identifiably near-[[Human/Legends|Human]] guise, clad in long flowing robes, with the hood thrown back to expose an intense demeanor. Always translucent, the Spirit protector increased in size as it moved in the young man's direction, until it seemed as though its mass had taken up the entire room instead of simply moving toward him. The protector restricted knowledge of the existence of its lore book to only those whom it deemed worthy. It chose to guide the hand of Shas Dovos, despite the contempt it initially held for the young man's arrogance, secretly advancing him in power and knowledge while he remained none the wiser. The spirit availed itself of Dovos' metallurgist talents and subtly manipulated him into the creation of what the protector referred to as "new skin." Even then, the spirit chose to reveal itself only after Dovos had proven himself suitable to the protector's purposes. Once visible, the spirit protector became extremely vocal and was moved to fits of sinister laughter at the terror its presence caused Dovos.<ref name="totjc" />

==Powers and abilities==
{{Quote|Without me you never could have understood the book, much less created the armor.|The spirit protector reveals its power as the source of Dovos' competence|<ref name="totjc" />}}
It was through the power of the spirit protector that the compendium to which it was restricted was able to withstand the ravages of time. Had it not been for its influence, the book would have disintegrated centuries prior to its discovery by Shas Dovos. Well-versed in Sith lore and magic, the spirit protector was also privy to the entirety of the book's secrets, and it refused to share them unless it felt the potential recipient worthy. It foretold Dovos' destiny as a champion in the quest to restore the Sith to [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] importance and was also skilled in the infusion of inanimate objects with dark side energies, knowledge that was imparted to Dovos. The protector was likewise able to permanently clad its apprentice in his magically-empowered armor. The ancient Sith spirit was able to enter minds and influence dreams or even compel beings into action. From bursts of flame to blinding flashes of light, [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoid]] to alien in likeness, the spirit protector was able to change its size, shape, and appearance at will.<ref name="totjc" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The spirit which inhabits the spellbook which Shas Dovos uses to craft the Warb Null armor is never named, and I don't name him here, but I can't help but see an aesthetic allusion to Adas in the design of Null's ebony armor&hellip;|Edward M. Erdelac|<ref name="hmt">{{WordPress|subdomain=emerdelac|name=Delirium Tremens: The Blog of Author Edward M. Erdelac|url=2014/01/21/hammer-time-star-wars-insider-148|text=Hammer Time! Star Wars Insider #147|author=Edward M. Erdelac|date=2014-01-21|archivedate=20200509185853}}</ref>}}
The spirit protector was first mentioned in Warb Null's entry in the ''[[Tales of the Jedi Companion]]'', a sourcebook for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'', published by [[West End Games]] in [[August]] [[1996]]. The protector is only referred to as "spirit protector," "protector," or "Sith spirit," with no definitive specification of [[Species/Legends|species]] other than "alien," and no [[Gender/Legends|gender]] or name.<ref name="totjc" /> The spirit protector was later mentioned in the entry for Warb Null in the [[2008]] release of ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II||Null, Warb}}</ref>

In his personal blog, ''[[Star Wars]]'' author [[Edward M. Erdelac]] noted that the design of Warb Null's battle armor may be seen as an aesthetic allusion to [[King/Legends|King]] [[Adas]], an ancient [[Sith'ari/Legends|Overlord]] of [[Korriban/Legends|Korriban]]<ref name="hmt" /> whose story was created by [[George R. Strayton]]<ref name="totjc" /> and developed by [[Abel G. Peña]].<ref name="end">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> For that reason, Erdelac theorizes that the spirit protector may have been that of the Overlord himself, which is why he included a vision of Adas in "[[Hammer (short story)|Hammer]],"<ref name="hmt" /> a short story in which a troubled [[Exploration Corps/Legends|Exploration Corps]] [[Malleus|member]] discovers and dons Null's armor.<ref name="Hammer" />
